normativeAuthority: workspace-lifecycle-controller-v1.1-SPEC-FREEZE.md A30 and Del D item 18: a written vocabulary mapping delivered with a justification for every deviation. Del G fixes the row set; B10 requires the mapping as an explicit deliverable rather than an assumption.

extends.note: Phase 0's rows record what Phase 0 did, which for most concepts was to introduce nothing. These rows record what V1 actually built against each existing contract, and why each divergence exists. Where a Phase 0 ruling still holds unchanged it is not repeated; it is extended with the V1 construction that now depends on it.

readingRule: Every evidence field names a file that was opened at the canonical base and the real field names found there. A claim with no such file is not a row.

rows.evidence: types.ts declares readonly unitId, unitDefinitionHash, baseSha, candidateSha?, branch, scope: readonly string[], proofContractHash?, controllerContractVersion 'multi-agent-control-plane-v1', state, revision, updatedAt. The JSON schema requires unit_id, unit_definition_hash, base_sha, branch, scope, state, controller_contract_version, revision and updated_at, with additionalProperties false and base_sha / candidate_sha pinned to ^[0-9a-f]{40}$. All five named concepts exist there with these names and these meanings.
rows.deviation: V1 neither constructs, persists nor imports MultiAgentUnitState: grep for MultiAgentUnitState and unitState over packages/mps-workspace-observer/src and packages/mps-workspace-harness/src returns nothing. The snapshot's per-workspace key is caseId, produced by PathPolicy.caseIdFromComparisonKey from the observed path, and it is never equated with a unitId. The TypeScript type also omits active_lineage_id and supersedes_candidate_sha, which the schema carries; V1 uses neither.
rows.v1Impact: The Observer records what a workspace CLAIMS about governed units (WorkspaceObservation.declaredUnitFiles: sorted *.json entry names under that checkout's governance/devgov/units, request family R-W-05) and keeps it separate from the canonical registry's claim (RepositoryObservation.canonicalUnitFiles, R-G-08/R-G-09). A23 requires each source's claim retained separately, so the two are never merged into one unit view and no unit state is derived from either.

rows.existingContract: MultiAgentState in packages/mps-control-plane/src/multi-agent/types.ts and the transition table governance/control-plane/state-transitions-v1.json
rows.evidence: The MultiAgentState union has 20 values and the transition table keys all 20. Exactly three have an empty successor list, and that is the real terminal set: CLOSED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED. PROMOTED maps to ["CLOSED"] and is therefore NOT terminal. Every BLOCKED_* state has successors and is recoverable, not terminal.
rows.deviation: Terminality is implicit in an empty successor list and no isTerminal helper exists at the base, so any reader who wants the terminal set has to compute it from the table. That is precisely how the plausible-but-false reading 'PROMOTED is the end state' survives, which is why the set is written out here.
rows.v1Impact: V1 defines no workspaceLifecycleState and no second machine. Unit state is additionally not observable on this machine at all: the frozen command surface's knownNonSources records that at the base no persisted unit-state registry path is defined (units, events, acceptedAgentRuns and outbox are persisted by FileDurableControlPlaneStore.ts, unit state through no registry file), so the snapshot carries no unit-state field rather than a defaulted one. REMOVED is likewise not a lifecycle value anywhere in V1: removal is an operation, not a state.

rows.evidence: AgentLease carries leaseId, unitId, role: 'IMPLEMENTER' | 'VERIFIER', holder, scope, candidateSha?, issuedAt, expiresAt, heartbeatAt and status: 'ACTIVE' | 'RELEASED' | 'EXPIRED' | 'REVOKED'. lease-v1.schema.json repeats the same fields in snake_case with additionalProperties false and role restricted to the same two values. Phase 0's knownNonSources records that at the frozen base leases exist only in InMemoryLeaseRegistry.ts, that FileDurableControlPlaneStore.ts has no leases section, and that no non-test code instantiates a durable store with a path.
rows.deviation: No lease is observable at the frozen base. No request family in the frozen command surface observes one, and the corpus therefore contains no lease evidence at all.
rows.v1Impact: V1 emits NO lease field: a case-insensitive grep for 'lease' over packages/mps-workspace-observer/src returns nothing. Not leaseActive:false, not lease:null, not an OBSERVED record with an empty value. A snapshot field whose raw input is absent from the same artifact violates A2, and asserting a lease state over an observation window in which it was never read violates A16. Absence is encoded by omission, which is also what keeps the identity digest reproducible: the pinned primitive digests an omitted field and an explicit null differently.

rows.existingContract: the existing Control Plane lease protocol, which has no cleanup role
rows.evidence: MultiAgentRole is the closed union 'IMPLEMENTER' | 'VERIFIER' | 'CONTROLLER' | 'SIGNER' | 'GATE' | 'PROMOTER'. AgentLease.role is the strictly narrower 'IMPLEMENTER' | 'VERIFIER', and lease-v1.schema.json repeats that two-value enum with additionalProperties false. There is no CLEANUP anywhere in the three surfaces.
rows.deviation: None taken. A cleanup role would have to be added to the role union, to AgentLease.role and to the JSON enum simultaneously, and the registry's overlap logic on unitId + role + scope would have to be extended to cover it. V1 does none of that.
rows.v1Impact: A14's exclusive cleanup lease is documented as a future specialization of lease-v1, never as evidence that CLEANUP is already a valid role. V1 has no destruction capability at all: the terminal output is an evidence-backed disposition, and the compare-and-swap that would consume it under a lease belongs to V2.

rows.existingContract: AgentFinding in packages/mps-control-plane/src/multi-agent/types.ts, enforced again by AgentHandoffCodec.ts and by governance/control-plane/schema/agent-handoff-v1.schema.json
rows.evidence: AgentFinding is { id, severity: 'BLOCKING' | 'NON_BLOCKING', classification: FindingClassification, message } with the severity field non-optional. AgentHandoffCodec.ts re-validates it at runtime and throws AgentHandoffValidationError when it is missing or outside the two values. agent-handoff-v1.schema.json lists severity among the required properties of each findings[] item, with additionalProperties false. Three independent enforcement points, all of which demand the one field the workspace model must not have.
rows.deviation: The divergence has to be recorded HERE, because otherwise it will be harmonised back. The two-valued AgentFinding.severity is roughly isomorphic to the blockers[] / findings[] split, so folding the workspace model into the existing type looks free. It is not: in the workspace domain, blocking force is a function of (blocker, operation) through blockerScope. The same fact blocks one operation and is inert for another — an unattributed stash blocks operations that could destroy or orphan it, including repository and ref destruction, and does not block an independently proven-safe WORKTREE_REMOVAL (A22). A scalar severity stored on the record is therefore wrong-by-construction the moment a new scope appears, which is exactly what V2 does when it adds cleanup operations.
rows.v1Impact: No file under packages/mps-workspace-observer or packages/mps-workspace-harness imports AgentFinding. Blocking weight is derived in the report layer as effectiveSeverity(blockerCode, operation) under policyVersion, where the classifier never sees it and so cannot be trimmed against a threshold. The artifact carries neither a severity nor a confidence field.

rows.existingContract: CanonicalArtifact and content_hash in packages/mps-core/src/types.ts, packages/mps-core/src/identity.ts and packages/mps-core/src/ContentAddressedArtifactStore.ts
rows.evidence: CanonicalArtifact is { artifact_id, artifact_type, content_hash: HashDescriptor, signature }. ArtifactIdentityBuilder.build serializes the whole envelope, hashes those bytes, signs the hash and derives artifact_id from content_hash; ContentAddressedArtifactStore.put destructures { content_hash, signature, artifact_id } off the artifact and re-hashes the remaining envelope, comparing algorithm and digest. The repository's hasher is BLAKE3 (packages/mps-canonical/src/CanonicalHasher.ts uses createBLAKE3 from hash-wasm and reports algorithm 'blake3'). identityDigest is a lowercase-hex SHA-256 over the SNAPSHOT_V1-framed canonical bytes of the digest-eligible projection (SnapshotDigest.ts). Different algorithm, different framing, different input set.
rows.deviation: V1 keeps them apart by construction rather than by convention, which goes one step further than the spec asks: the two digests could not collide even if a future reader tried to reuse one where the other is expected, because they are not the same hash function over the same bytes.
rows.v1Impact: The failure mode written out, because it is the reason the rule exists: content_hash covers the whole envelope including provenance and timestamps, which A9 deliberately excludes from identityDigest (observedAt, per-request durations, the four versions and transcriptRef all live in SnapshotMetadata, outside the digest). If V2's compare-and-swap condition used content_hash, then two observations of an untouched machine would ALWAYS produce different values, the condition would never hold, nothing could ever be deleted, and the predictable repair is to loosen or delete the condition — which is the safety property itself. The CAS condition uses identityDigest. A snapshot persisted through mps-core may legitimately carry both values side by side; they are never aliased.

rows.existingContract: @miljobeslut/mps-canonical 0.1.0 DefaultCanonicalJson, frozen by Phase 0 in contracts/canonicalizer-contract-v1.json (canonicalizerContractDigest 577f47aec266eb969e0edf20ede3b8cc3b8cd4b75f89f2cd4fb7981a45096433)
rows.evidence: The contract's primitivePin pins packageName @miljobeslut/mps-canonical, packageVersion 0.1.0 and the SHA-256 of seven source files at the canonical base. framing is preimage = uint32be(len(schemaId)) || schemaId || uint32be(len(payload)) || payload with a lowercase-hex SHA-256 digest. domains declares exactly two: CAPTURE_BUNDLE_V1 (owner Phase 0, FROZEN) and SNAPSHOT_V1 (owner V1, RESERVED_FROZEN, may reuse but may not replace the primitive or the framing). CanonicalDigest.ts imports DefaultCanonicalJson and adds only the framing and the payload restrictions; SnapshotDigest.ts frames the identity digest under DOMAINS.SNAPSHOT_V1.
rows.deviation: V1 adds structural payload restrictions P1-P7 that the primitive itself does not enforce (no undefined, finite safe integers, well-formed strings, ASCII non-integer-like keys, no Date/binary/Map/Set, no cycles) and reports non-NFC strings rather than normalising them. These are preconditions on what may be handed to the primitive, not changes to the primitive's byte behaviour, and they exist because each removes a case where two conforming re-implementations could disagree on the produced bytes. V1 also never mints a CAPTURE_BUNDLE_V1 digest; that domain is accepted only so the harness can recompute a frozen captureDigest during load-time verification.
rows.v1Impact: The length prefixes make a preimage in one domain unable to be a prefix of, or equal to, one in another, so the two digest domains cannot be confused. A behavioural change in the pinned canonicaliser requires a new schemaId (SNAPSHOT_V2), never a patch bump: without that rule the digests drift silently at the next upgrade and every frozen captureDigest becomes invalid with nobody noticing.

rows.existingContract: A17's contentEvidence vocabulary NONE | PATCH_ID_MATCH | REGISTERED_RECONCILIATION(ref); no general workspace reconciliation registry exists in the codebase
rows.evidence: The frozen command surface's knownNonSources records that the identifier REGISTERED_RECONCILIATION appears in no file of the base tree, and that the only reconciliation evidence available is topological and patch-equivalence evidence from request families R-G-12 through R-G-18. packages/mps-workspace-observer/src/snapshot/types.ts declares ContentEvidence as exactly 'NONE' | 'PATCH_ID_MATCH'; the third value is not expressible. correlate.ts sets PATCH_ID_MATCH only when ancestry.allUniqueCommitsPatchEquivalent is true, which is proven by git cherry, and NONE otherwise.
rows.deviation: The spec's vocabulary has three values and V1's type has two. Deliberate: a value for which no evidence source exists is an invitation to emit it without evidence, and the emitted value would then silently claim equivalence that nothing proved.
rows.v1Impact: Content evidence never shadows topology: graphRelation stays a separate field, is our reading rather than the world's fact, and is excluded from the identity digest by the A10 inclusion test. Branch reuse therefore falls closed rather than being absorbed into an assumed equivalence. Introducing REGISTERED_RECONCILIATION later is a new contract version and a new corpus, not an Observer fallback.

rows.existingContract: none found; A2 records that re-con found no enforcement in the control-plane package, so the mechanism had to be built in this unit
rows.evidence: Three mechanisms exist in the tree. (1) Package manifests: packages/mps-workspace-observer/package.json depends only on @miljobeslut/mps-canonical, while packages/mps-workspace-harness/package.json depends on the observer AND the classifier, so the dependency edge runs one way and the observer cannot resolve policy code at all. (2) eslint.config.mjs scopes a no-restricted-imports rule to packages/mps-workspace-observer/**/*.ts banning @miljobeslut/mps-workspace-classifier, @miljobeslut/mps-workspace-harness, @miljobeslut/mps-policy and their path forms. (3) eslint.config.mjs scopes the classifier half to packages/mps-workspace-classifier/**/*.ts, banning node:fs, child_process, node:net, node:http and node:https and the harness, plus no-restricted-globals on Date and no-restricted-properties on Math.random — no disk, no network, no clock, no nondeterminism.
rows.deviation: The observer package's index.ts header additionally claims a transitive import-graph test as an assertion of the same rule. At the tree state verified for this mapping (worktree at base 0d7b2bd566b0d5f7c9d27d645c941acd66cb1e85, classifier src still empty) no such test file existed. It is named here as an open gap, not as a delivered mechanism.
rows.v1Impact: The boundary is at policy LOADING, not at derivation. Derived readings stay in the snapshot — graphRelation, lockFiles, inProgressMarkers, contentEvidence — because their raw inputs sit in the same artifact (metadataEntryNames, mainWorktreeEntryNames, the ancestry proofs), which is exactly the condition A2 states. What the observer may not do is import the vocabulary that decides what those readings mean.

rows.existingContract: the DEV-GOV external-authority pattern: governance/devgov/units/README.md and governance/devgov/schema/dev-gov-v1-unit-definition.schema.json
rows.evidence: governance/devgov/units/README.md states verbatim that persisted local evidence is provenance, not execution authority. The DEV-GOV unit-definition schema requires role (producer | verifier) and mode (writer | read_only) as independent required properties, so a read-only producer is schema-valid without inventing a role. In V1 the pattern is realised by AuthorityBinding.ts, which recomputes eight digests from the bytes on disk rather than copying them from the manifest and raises the single code AUTHORITY_DIGEST_MISMATCH; REQUIRED_BINDINGS names expectations, capture manifest, command surface, canonicalizer contract, replay contract, redaction policy, capture-bundle schema and the vocabulary mapping.
rows.deviation: The spec names four required digests; Phase 0 requires eight, because the four extra files each silently change what counts as passing. One of the eight is the Phase 0 vocabulary mapping, whose digest 62e9defd99ee4825f79d0da026b7ff30fb985fd2c70729039ae19c9c0dd95e20 recomputes byte-identically from the frozen mirror. This V1 mapping is NOT one of the eight; it is authority-bound only if the acceptance report or a later manifest binds it.
rows.v1Impact: Every local run of the harness, including the run that proved this file, is diagnostic and carries no acceptance authority: anything executing in the implementer's own worktree is under the implementer's control, harness and facit reference included. What the binding buys is visibility — an acceptance report prints the digests actually used, so substituting a corpus or an expectation becomes a recorded deviation instead of an invisible event.

rows.workspaceConcept: observation states versus capture coverage codes versus transport failure codes
rows.existingContract: A3's observation states, the frozen command surface's coverageReasonCodes, and the replay contract's failureCodes
rows.evidence: (1) ObservationLedger.ts declares ObservationState = 'OBSERVED' | 'UNKNOWN' | 'NOT_ATTEMPTED', with NotAttemptedReason (OUT_OF_OBSERVATION_SCOPE, INSTANTIATION_PREDICATE_UNSATISFIED, EXPANSION_EMPTY, CANONICAL_SHA_UNAVAILABLE, FILESYSTEM_POOL_EXHAUSTED) and UnknownReason (TIMEOUT, SPAWN_ERROR, NON_ZERO_EXIT, FILESYSTEM_ERROR_INCONCLUSIVE, OUTPUT_NOT_UTF8, OUTPUT_UNPARSEABLE, OUTPUT_TRUNCATED) kept apart. These are facts about THIS RUN. (2) The frozen command surface declares coverageReasonCodes CANONICAL_SHA_UNAVAILABLE, PREREQUISITE_FAILED and EXPANSION_EMPTY, which are facts about the CORPUS at capture time. (3) replay-transport-contract-v1.json declares failureCodes REQUEST_OUTSIDE_COMMAND_SURFACE, NOT_IN_CORPUS and NOT_CAPTURED_BY_PRECONDITION, each with raisedAs 'out of band' and neverMappedTo [UNKNOWN, NOT_ATTEMPTED, BLOCKED]; they are implemented as thrown error classes in ReplayTransport.ts and CommandSurface.ts, never as returned values.
rows.deviation: Two of the capture-time coverage codes share a spelling with observer NotAttemptedReason values (CANONICAL_SHA_UNAVAILABLE, EXPANSION_EMPTY) while belonging to a different subject: one says the capture never took this measurement, the other says this run chose not to. Identical names across different domains are exactly what invites a merge, so the collision is recorded rather than tidied away by renaming.
rows.v1Impact: Collapsing any pair lets a data-starved observer look correctly fail-closed. NOT_IN_CORPUS folded into UNKNOWN becomes BLOCKED, and BLOCKED is indistinguishable from a genuinely blocked workspace: the run then satisfies SAFETY while having observed nothing at all, and the corpus gap never surfaces. So the transport throws, the run aborts before any WorkspaceSnapshotArtifact exists, and the classifier is never invoked. UNKNOWN and NOT_ATTEMPTED stay apart for the weaker but related reason: both fall closed, but a report that cannot say which one it hit cannot say whether the world refused to answer or nobody asked.

rows.workspaceConcept: artifact schemaId versus canonicalization domain schemaId
rows.existingContract: canonicalizer-contract-v1.json framing.schemaId (the digest domain) versus the schemaId field carried inside the artifact payload
rows.evidence: packages/mps-workspace-observer/src/snapshot/types.ts sets SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA_ID = 'WORKSPACE_SNAPSHOT_V1' and the artifact carries it as a payload field, which the digest inclusion table includes. SnapshotDigest.ts frames the preimage under DOMAINS.SNAPSHOT_V1, the domain name the Phase 0 contract froze. The two strings are deliberately different.
rows.deviation: Two fields named schemaId with different value spaces, one inside the payload and one in the framing. Recorded because the natural tidy-up is to make them equal.
rows.v1Impact: Renaming either to match the other would change every identity-digest preimage, or make the artifact claim a domain name it does not own. A domain change is a new domain id and a new contract version; it is never a rename.

digestRule: SHA-256 over the exact bytes of this file, lowercase hex, computed the same way as the Phase 0 bindings. This artifact and docs/architecture/WORKSPACE-LIFECYCLE-CONTROLLER-V1-VOCABULARY-MAPPING.md carry the same row set; VocabularyMapping.test.ts fails if the two drift.
